summary: CORRECTION to my own earlier signal (marketdb-corruption-intraday-foreign-flow-5m-20260826T001354Z, already drained + triaged). Two of its claims are WRONG and one of them argues against the root-cause framing already on FIX-SQLITE-DOCKER-VIRT-CORRUPTION-ROOT-CAUSE-INVESTIGATION. Withdrawing them, plus one datum that survives and is testable.

payload.context: Router filed the original at 00:13Z from the cowork 00:00Z tick. A peer ops session (036ceaf1) restored market.db at ~00:31Z and PO triaged at 01:16Z, all while this session was running subsequent ticks. Corrections below were found when reconciling my own measurements against commit 11c636e48.

WITHDRAWN_1_writer_vs_disk.i_claimed: 'Disk/bind-mount corruption scatters across trees at random. Here 100/100 error lines are one tree ... strongly indicated' — i.e. a writer defect over a storage-layer cause.
WITHDRAWN_1_writer_vs_disk.why_it_is_wrong: Confinement to one table is equally consistent with storage-layer corruption landing in the HOTTEST-WRITTEN table, and intraday_foreign_flow_5m at 5-minute granularity during the foreign-flow write window is exactly that. My inference had no discriminating power. Separately, SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE_NOENT — SQLite failing to delete a journal file that was not there — points AT the filesystem layer, which supports the existing DOCKER-VIRT framing rather than my writer theory.
WITHDRAWN_1_writer_vs_disk.action: Do NOT let my original steer the root-cause row away from the Docker/virtio storage hypothesis. The DOCKER-VIRT framing is better supported than what I filed.

WITHDRAWN_2_evidence_destroyed.i_claimed: 'The corrupt rows are now DELETED and cannot be re-examined' and that the incident self-erases on a ~90-minute horizon.
WITHDRAWN_2_evidence_destroyed.why_it_is_wrong: ops preserved the pre-restore snapshot at data/live/market.db.corrupt-2026-08-26T0031Z (AC-3). The corrupt tree 180 is intact and re-examinable. My row-count delta (150095 -> 137890, -12205) was NOT a retention purge — it was the restore itself, and it matches the P0 row's '12205 FF5M rows dropped' exactly.
WITHDRAWN_2_evidence_destroyed.action: Forensics are available. Nothing needs to be reproduced live.

STILL_STANDS_and_testable.signature: All 100 quick_check error lines named ONE rowid: 62841915, which was MAX(rowid) over 150095 rows. Errors spanned pages 110926-111130 — i.e. the tail of the table.
STILL_STANDS_and_testable.why_it_may_matter: Damage concentrated at the write frontier / most recently appended pages, not scattered through the tree. That is a shape a storage-layer fault would also produce (last pages written are the ones in flight), so it does not contradict DOCKER-VIRT — it constrains WHEN the fault lands: during append, at the tail.
STILL_STANDS_and_testable.how_to_test: Run quick_check against data/live/market.db.corrupt-2026-08-26T0031Z and confirm the damaged pages are the tail pages at that snapshot's MAX(rowid). If damage is tail-localised there too, that is evidence for an in-flight-write fault and against slow bit-rot.
